findings.claim: §6 manifest-integrity wording overstates the protection provided by CODEOWNERS after slice 020K: it implies enforced CODEOWNERS review from 020K onward, but GitHub only blocks PRs on missing CODEOWNERS approval when `require_code_owner_reviews: true` is set in branch protection — a flag that is absent from both WP-SCP-020 §4 020D2's explicit branch-protection settings and any other plan section. Until `require_code_owner_reviews: true` is active (which requires an explicit branch-protection API call not currently mandated by 020D2), CODEOWNERS review is requested but not enforced, meaning the manifest remains unprotected for the full 020K-to-020D2 window. The claim 'closes R3 BYPASS-005 carry-forward' may therefore be premature.
findings.evidence: §6 text (plan lines 549-555): 'the pin manifest path is added to `CODEOWNERS` (slice 020K) so any change to the manifest requires a CODEOWNERS reviewer. Until 020K lands, manual operator vigilance is the only check.' Implies enforced protection begins at 020K. WP-SCP-020 §4 020D2 description (lines 119, 177): explicitly lists `required_approving_review_count=1`, `dismiss_stale_reviews: true`, `require_review_from_non_author=false` — `require_code_owner_reviews` is not listed. Grep of docs/plans/ for 'require_code_owner_reviews' returns zero matches in any plan document. GitHub REST API: the branch-protection `required_pull_request_reviews.require_code_owner_reviews` field is a distinct boolean from `required_approving_review_count` (GitHub branch-protection PUT payload schema). Without it set to `true`, a PR touching `acc-pin-manifest.json` can merge with any one approval, regardless of CODEOWNERS.
findings.impact: The manifest-integrity window that BYPASS-005 targeted extends from plan-merge all the way to 020D2 (not just to 020K) if `require_code_owner_reviews: true` is never set. A tampered acc-pin-manifest.json committed on an implementation slice's feature branch would pass the gate helper (which detects ACC drift vs manifest, not manifest tampering), and if the manifest points to attacker-controlled blob SHAs, the dispatcher would fetch and execute scripts from an untrusted ACC revision without alerting the chain. The wording 'manual operator vigilance is the only check' before 020K is correct but the implicit claim of enforced protection after 020K is misleading and could cause the operator to relax vigilance prematurely.
findings.mitigation: Either (a) add `require_code_owner_reviews: true` explicitly to the 020D2 branch-protection API call (amend WP-SCP-020 §4 020D2 slice description and the WP-SCP-022 §6 wording), OR (b) correct the §6 wording to read: 'Until 020D2 lands (which enables required reviews on main including code-owner review enforcement via require_code_owner_reviews: true), manual operator vigilance is the only check against manifest tampering; CODEOWNERS (020K) requests review but GitHub does not enforce it without the branch-protection flag.' AND update the BYPASS-005 closure claim accordingly. Option (a) is preferred — it closes the actual gap rather than just documenting it.

findings.claim: R-022-13 specifies two mandatory `verify_commands` for slice 020J's dispatch package to prevent partial-apply leaving the SCP repo in an inconsistently-protected state, but this requirement is not referenced in §9 autonomous-run-complete acceptance criteria and is absent from WP-SCP-020 §4's 020J slice description. An orchestrator building the 020J dispatch package who reads §9 and WP-SCP-020 §4 (the normal spec_paths path) would not be told to include these specific verify_commands, defeating the partial-apply protection.
findings.evidence: §8 R-022-13 (plan lines 669-693): '**20J `verify_commands`** must include both: `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/tags/protection | jq '\''.[]\ | select(.pattern=="v*")'\''` returning a single match, and `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection/required_signatures | jq '\'' .enabled'\''` returning `true`. Either verify failing → exit non-zero → dispatcher status overridden to `blocked`.' §9 autonomous-run-complete criteria (plan lines 719-733): enumerates 12-PR Track 1 merge, release-signoff.md, USER-GATE-A.md, 4-PR Track 2 merge, USER-GATE-C.md, evidence directories, required check live, PyPI installable. No mention of 020J verify_commands per R-022-13. WP-SCP-020 §4 020J slice description (line 113): describes tag-protection rule + required-signed-commits but specifies no verify_commands. §4.1 dispatch package contract (lines 261-264): states verify_commands is non-empty and 'Always includes `pytest`'; for workflow slices includes actionlint; for Rego slices includes conftest/opa test — no mention of 020J-specific API verify commands.
findings.impact: 020J is the highest-blast-radius slice in the WP: it makes two irreversible GitHub API calls against a live production repo (v* tag-protection + main required-signed-commits). A partial-apply leaves SCP main in an inconsistently-protected state where subsequent slices (020D1 onward) assume signed commits are enforced on main but they are not. If the 020J dispatch package's verify_commands omit the two specific `gh api` checks from R-022-13, the dispatcher could report `status=complete` on a partial-apply without the chain detecting it. The partial-apply revert logic (R-022-13(c)) also only triggers if Codex was instructed to implement it — which requires the 020J instruction to explicitly cite R-022-13.
findings.mitigation: Add an explicit AC to §9 autonomous-run-complete: '[ ] Slice 020J dispatch package verify_commands include both API checks per §8 R-022-13 (tag-protection match and required_signatures.enabled=true); gate helper rejects 020J dispatch package if either check is absent.' Additionally, cross-reference §8 R-022-13 from §4.1's verify_commands guidance (e.g. 'for the 020J tag-protection + signed-commits slice, verify_commands are specified in §8 R-022-13') so orchestrators building the 020J package cannot miss it. Optionally, add the two verify commands to the WP-SCP-020 §4 020J slice description so they survive if the spec_paths reference omits WP-SCP-022.
